clue.text: All-thirsty giant has to gasp to get a semi-liquid diet

parts.note: to gasp is to pant for breath
gruel is a thin porridge, a semi-liquid food for invalids

explanation.surface: A parched giant, panting, is fed nothing but porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabelais's giant's name was glossed as meaning 'all-thirsty', which is why the definition reads so oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabelais named his giant from Greek roots taken to mean 'all' and 'thirsty', so the description identifies the character.

clue.text: So far and, no further, Moon!

definitions.text: So far and, no further, Moon!

parts.words: So far and, no further, Moon!
parts.note: a command to the Moon to go only so far out and no further, naming the outermost point of its orbit

explanation.surface: Someone orders the Moon to stop wandering off.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is the point in an orbit where the Moon is farthest from the Earth.

clue.text: Boss 'of the Latin Quarter

parts.note: read as the ruler of one quarter of a province in the Latin-speaking Roman world, not the Paris student district

explanation.surface: A gang leader who runs the student district of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin Quarter suggests Paris; the clue means a Roman governor of a quarter of a province, as Herod Antipas was.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman Empire this title was given to a ruler of a fourth part of a province.

clue.text: No poached eggs if he knows his onions

definitions.text: No poached eggs if he knows his onions

parts.words: No poached eggs if he knows his onions
parts.note: the estate worker who guards game birds will let no eggs be stolen by poachers if he knows his job

explanation.surface: A cook's boast that a competent chef never ruins poached eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poached' looks like cooking; it means taken illegally by poachers. 'Knows his onions' is an idiom for being expert.
explanation.definitionFit: This estate worker protects pheasants and their eggs from poachers.

clue.text: Parvenu's blast-off ?

definitions.meaning: a parvenu is a social climber newly risen to wealth
a rocket's blast-off is when it starts going up

explanation.surface: A newly rich social climber is launched like a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A social climber suddenly risen in rank is called this; split in two, the word describes a launch heading skywards.

clue.text: Do nothing but listen to Macaulay's work

indicators.note: listening means the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Lord Macaulay wrote the Lays of Ancient Rome, a book of ballads

explanation.surface: Someone idles about, doing nothing but listening to readings of a historian's book.
explanation.definitionFit: To lounge idly is to do nothing at all.

clue.text: Shell-burst reveals this flat-footed Australian

parts.note: an egg-laying Australian animal whose Greek name means 'flat foot' hatches from a bursting shell

explanation.surface: A clumsy Australian soldier is exposed by an exploding artillery shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell-burst' suggests war; it is an egg hatching, since this mammal lays eggs. Its name comes from Greek for 'flat foot'.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck-billed mammal of Australia lays eggs and its name is Greek for flat-footed.

clue.text: One bound to admit that America favours him

parts.note: pro means in favour of
the man speaking of himself would say me
America is the US, with the article: the US

explanation.surface: A captive confesses that the United States is on his side.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken by the man himself, 'America favours him' becomes 'pro me the US'. The Titan who stole fire was chained to a rock, so 'One bound' defines him.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titan who gave fire to mankind was chained to a rock as punishment, the subject of Aeschylus's play about him bound.

clue.text: No straightforward sportsman ?

parts.note: a fisherman with a hook and line, playing on the hook being bent rather than straight

explanation.surface: A sportsman who is less than honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straightforward' looks like honesty; this sportsman uses a crooked hook, an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman using rod and line pursues this sport, named from the old word for a hook.

clue.text: Involving some cuts in dress-making

indicators.note: to involve is literally to roll up or entangle, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Tailoring requires some cutting of the cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' rolls up the letters of 'some cuts' into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Outfits made for the stage are the products of a dressmaker's work.

clue.text: Where one drives to the stomach to become top?

parts.note: in golf one drives off from the tee
tum is an informal word for the stomach

explanation.surface: A golfer heads for the tee as a way of getting on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Golf imagery hides a toy: a small spinning top with lettered sides.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small spinning top with lettered sides, used in games of chance.

clue.text: In France I return to scoff

annotationWithheld.why: 'In France I return to scoff' (4) for JEER: JE is French for I, but no clue word gives ER except 'return' itself, which would have to be both the letters RE and the reversal indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: In France I return to scoff

clue.text: Vorpal blade's victim one frabjous day

definitions.text: Vorpal blade's victim one frabjous day

parts.words: Vorpal blade's victim one frabjous day
parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem the hero's vorpal sword slays the monster on a frabjous day

explanation.surface: A line of nonsense verse about a slaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's monster in Through the Looking-Glass is killed by the hero's vorpal sword.

clue.text: 'ark at the instrument close to the drum

definitions.text: 'ark at the instrument close to the drum

parts.words: 'ark at the instrument close to the drum
parts.note: hark, in Cockney speech, at a hearing aid held close to the eardrum

explanation.surface: A Cockney tells you to listen to a horn player beside the drummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The band picture misleads: the drum is the eardrum, and 'ark is hark, listen, which is what this horn helps the deaf to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A horn-shaped hearing aid funnels sound towards the eardrum of a deaf listener.

clue.text: This man met centain difficulty — in a postal strike?

definitions.text: This man met centain difficulty — in a postal strike?

indicators.note: the words meet difficulty, so their letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the printed 'centain' is a misprint for 'certain'

explanation.surface: A man living on money sent from home is stranded when the post stops.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange 'met certain' (printed 'centain', a misprint). A remittance man lived abroad on money posted from home, so a postal strike stops his income.
explanation.definitionFit: Money sent by post to someone abroad is the thing a postal strike would hold up, and a man living on it is named for it.

clue.text: Occupiers of squares and palaces

parts.note: chess pieces sit on squares of the board, and senior clergy live in episcopal palaces

explanation.surface: Wealthy residents of town squares and grand houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Squares suggests town planning; it means the chessboard, where these pieces move diagonally, and the same churchmen live in palaces.
explanation.definitionFit: These pieces move diagonally on a chessboard, and the churchmen of the same name traditionally reside in palaces.

clue.text: One in eleven is a deputy churchwarden

definitions.meaning: a member of a cricket team of eleven
an assistant to the churchwarden who takes the collection

explanation.surface: A cricketer doubles as a parish official.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket side has eleven players, so one of them is a side's man.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant churchwarden who shows people to pews bears this title, which also splits into a team member.

clue.text: Admission of a has-been to a' dead end

definitions.meaning: someone past their best confessing they are out of date and no longer fashionable

explanation.surface: A washed-up figure confesses he has nowhere left to go.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M PASSÉ, it is what a has-been admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock from which no progress is possible is a figurative blind alley.

clue.text: Pooh-Bah's first was a protoplasmal primordial atomic globule

definitions.text: Pooh-Bah's first was a protoplasmal primordial atomic globule

parts.words: Pooh-Bah's first was a protoplasmal primordial atomic globule
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, Pooh-Bah boasts of tracing his family line back to a primordial globule

explanation.surface: A quotation about the snobbish official from The Mikado.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooh-Bah, in the comic opera The Mikado, claims he can trace his descent back to a 'protoplasmal primordial atomic globule'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of one's forebears is a forefather in one's family line.

clue.text: Bloomers made with £25 bets round Mile End

indicators.note: the bets go round, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

indicators.note: the end of Mile is its last letter

explanation.surface: Underwear bought with gambling winnings in a district of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Mile End is an East London district; here it is just the last letter of 'Mile'. 'Bloomers' looks like underwear but means flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that bloom are flowers, and these showy garden blooms are an example.

clue.text: Tender name — maybe Darling

indicators.note: maybe says the words could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A term of affection such as 'darling' is a tender name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a definition of the answer; the letters of 'Tender name' rearranged give it, and 'Darling' is the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone darling is a term of affection, an example of the thing.

clue.text: Some rate this the luck of the Irish

definitions.meaning: a local tax or levy, a kind of rate
in the Irish curse 'bad ... to you' the word means luck

explanation.surface: Some people value Irish luck highly.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a tax or levy, it also means fortune in the Irish phrase 'bad luck to you'.

clue.text: Hail may be general

definitions.meaning: a general ... is a military honour paid to royalty

explanation.surface: A storm of hail could be widespread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like weather; it means greet, and 'general' is not 'widespread' but the military ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting with a raised hand is this, and a formal military mark of respect can be a general one.

clue.text: No, elsewhere but not here is backing for a churchman

indicators.note: backing means the whole string of letters is read from the end to the start

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

indicators.note: but not means the following word is taken out

explanation.surface: Someone says no, it is elsewhere, not here, that supports a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not here' leaves ELSEW; 'is backing' reverses NAY + ELSEW, giving NAYELSEW backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of John Wesley belongs to the Methodist church.

clue.text: A dry sort of measure

indicators.note: to sort the letters is to arrange them differently

explanation.surface: A measure of liquor served dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the letters of 'A dry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Three feet make this imperial unit of length.

clue.text: A suiting made up for a Jesuit

indicators.note: the letters are made up into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A tailored suit is made for a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' looks like tailoring; it rearranges 'A suiting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignatius Loyola founded the Society of Jesus, so the first member of the order bore this name.

clue.text: Boxing his job ? Here the end of a meteoric career?

definitions.meaning: a man whose job is packing goods into boxes

definitions.text: Here the end of a meteoric career
definitions.meaning: a meteorite ends its flight in the hollow it gouges in the ground

explanation.surface: A boxer's job, and a meteoric career that comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' suggests prize-fighting; it means packing into boxes, so one who does it.
explanation.definitionFit: A packer of goods into crates is so named, and a meteorite leaves a bowl-shaped hollow where it lands.

clue.text: 501. cut by 10 will lower morale

parts.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and I is 1
to shear is to cut
ten is the number

explanation.surface: Losing 10 from 501 in darts would dishearten a player.
explanation.walkthrough: 501 is written in Roman numerals; 'by' only sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage people is to sap their spirits and confidence.
